# Windjammer (full context for LLM agents)

> Windjammer is a high-level language that compiles to Rust, with ownership and borrowing inferred by the compiler. The same `.wj` source also runs in an interpreter and has Go, JavaScript and WebAssembly backends of lower maturity.

Version 0.50.0. Assembled by `scripts/docs_gen.sh` from the files named in each section heading; do not edit. Index version: llms.txt.


---

# Source: docs/agent/WINDJAMMER_FOR_AGENTS.md

## Windjammer for agents

Windjammer (`.wj`) is a Rust-family language with inferred ownership: you write `fn f(x: Vec<int>)`, the compiler
decides borrow/move/clone. You have almost certainly seen no Windjammer in training. Do not guess from Rust or
Python: look things up (`wj docs <terms>`), and check every edit. Every code block below is executed by CI.

### The loop

<!-- ignore: command shapes with FILE/DIR placeholders; every subcommand and flag is checked against the CLI by the links check -->
```bash,ignore
wj check --json FILE_OR_DIR     # parse + lint + transpile, no cargo; JSON diagnostics with spans
wj run --interpret FILE         # instant run, no cargo/rustc; stdout is program output only
wj test --interpret DIR         # runs @test and test_* functions in *_test.wj
wj build FILE                   # production path (transpiles to Rust, then cargo)
wj docs hashmap entry           # offline search: stdlib, built-ins, idioms, 150+ verified examples
wj explain WJ0001               # error code explanation
wj fmt FILE                     # formatter; wj lint FILE checks Rust-isms; wj fix PATH migrates them
```

Exit status of a program: 0 ok, 101 panic, N for `process::exit(N)`, 2 means "unsupported in the interpreter".
`wj check` passing does not mean `wj run --interpret` passes, and the interpreter accepts more than `wj build`
(see "Compiled path gaps").

### Core idioms

Types: `int` (64-bit), `float` (f64), `bool`, `string`, `char`, `Vec<T>`, `Option<T>`, `Result<T, E>`,
`HashMap<K, V>`. Locals are immutable unless `let mut`. The last expression of a block is its value; do not write
`return` at the end of a function. Strings interpolate with `${expr}`, with format specs after a colon.

```windjammer
// expect: Ada is 36; pi=3.14; [   42]; [00042]; Some(3)
fn main() {
    let name = "Ada"
    let age = 36
    let mut parts: Vec<string> = []
    parts.push("${name} is ${age}")
    parts.push("pi=${3.14159:.2}")
    parts.push("[${42:>5}]")
    parts.push("[${42:05}]")
    parts.push("${Some(3):?}")
    println(parts.join("; "))
}
```

`println`, `print`, `panic`, `assert`, `assert_eq`, `assert_ne`, `todo`, `debug` are plain functions, not macros.
There are no semicolons. `if`, `match` and blocks are expressions.

```windjammer
// expect: small
// expect: 7
fn size(n: int) -> string {
    if n < 10 { "small" } else if n < 100 { "medium" } else { "large" }
}

fn main() {
    println(size(3))
    let best = { let a = 3
        let b = 7
        if a > b { a } else { b } }
    println("${best}")
}
```

### Structs, enums, traits

Methods take plain `self`; whether it is read-only, mutating or consuming is inferred from the body. Mutating a
receiver still requires the caller to hold it in a `let mut`. Derives (Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Copy) are inferred:
never write `#[derive(...)]`.

```windjammer
// expect: Rect(3x4) area=12
// expect: Rect(6x4) area=24
// expect: Circle r=2
struct Rect { w: int, h: int }

impl Rect {
    fn area(self) -> int { self.w * self.h }
    fn show(self) -> string { "Rect(${self.w}x${self.h}) area=${self.area()}" }
    fn widen(self, by: int) { self.w += by }
}

trait Named {
    fn label(self) -> string
}

struct Circle { r: int }

impl Named for Circle {
    fn label(self) -> string { "Circle r=${self.r}" }
}

fn main() {
    let mut r = Rect { w: 3, h: 4 }
    println(r.show())
    r.widen(3)
    println(r.show())
    println(Circle { r: 2 }.label())
}
```

Enums carry data and are consumed with exhaustive `match`; arms may have guards and or-patterns. Range patterns
(`1..=9`) are not supported yet: use a guard.

```windjammer
// expect: Circle 12
// expect: Rect 6
// expect: big
enum Shape {
    Circle(int),
    Rect(int, int),
}

fn describe(s: Shape) -> string {
    match s {
        Shape::Circle(r) => "Circle ${r * r * 3}",
        Shape::Rect(w, h) => "Rect ${w * h}",
    }
}

fn bucket(n: int) -> string {
    match n {
        0 | 1 => "tiny",
        x if x < 100 => "mid",
        _ => "big",
    }
}

fn main() {
    println(describe(Shape::Circle(2)))
    println(describe(Shape::Rect(2, 3)))
    println(bucket(1000))
}
```

### Error handling

Use `Option`/`Result`, `match`, `?`, `unwrap_or`, `map_err`, `ok_or`. `.unwrap()` and `.expect()` are lint errors
(W0002), so `wj build` rejects them. `?` propagates `Err`/`None` from the enclosing function.

```windjammer
// expect: Ok(10)
// expect: Err("bad: x")
// expect: 0
fn parse(s: string) -> Result<int, string> {
    s.parse::<int>().map_err(|_| "bad: ${s}")
}

fn double(s: string) -> Result<int, string> {
    let n = parse(s)?
    Ok(n * 2)
}

fn main() {
    println("${double("5"):?}")
    println("${double("x"):?}")
    let n: Option<int> = None
    println("${n.unwrap_or(0)}")
}
```

`Result` and `Option` do not implement Display: print with `${x:?}` or `match` first. Custom error types are plain
enums (see `wj docs error enum`).

### Collections and iteration

`let v = [1, 2, 3]` is a growable `Vec`. Iterate directly: `for x in v`, `for (i, x) in v.enumerate()`. Adapter
chains start from the collection itself: write `v.map(..)`, not `v.iter().map(..)` (`.iter()` is lint error W0003).
Maps need `use std::collections::HashMap`; iteration order of a `HashMap` is unspecified, so sort keys before printing.

```windjammer
// expect: [1, 4, 9]
// expect: 6
// expect: a=1 b=2
// expect: 0:x 1:y
use std::collections::HashMap

fn main() {
    let v = [1, 2, 3]
    let squares: Vec<int> = v.map(|x| x * x).collect()
    println("${squares:?}")
    println("${v.sum::<int>()}")
    let mut m: HashMap<string, int> = HashMap::new()
    m.insert("b", 2)
    m.insert("a", 1)
    let mut keys: Vec<string> = m.keys().collect()
    keys.sort()
    let mut out: Vec<string> = []
    for k in keys { out.push("${k}=${m[k]}") }
    println(out.join(" "))
    let mut line: Vec<string> = []
    for (i, s) in ["x", "y"].enumerate() { line.push("${i}:${s}") }
    println(line.join(" "))
}
```

The pipe operator feeds the left value into a call: `x |> f(a)` is `f(x, a)`; `x |> .method(a)` is `x.method(a)`.
It has the lowest precedence, so `a + 1 |> f` is `f(a + 1)`. A trailing `?` applies to that stage.

```windjammer
// expect: 16
// expect: [2, 4, 6]
fn double(x: int) -> int { x * 2 }
fn add(x: int, y: int) -> int { x + y }

fn main() {
    println("${3 |> add(5) |> double}")
    let d: Vec<int> = [1, 2, 3] |> .map(|x| x * 2) |> .collect()
    println("${d:?}")
}
```

### Modules and tests

Inline `mod name { pub fn .. }` and one-file-per-module (`a.wj` or `a/mod.wj`, found next to the importer or in the
project root/`src/`) are both resolved with `use a::f`; paths use `::`. Tests live in `*_test.wj`: `@test`, `test_*`
functions, or `@test_cases([(in, expected), ...])` with one parameter per tuple field.

```windjammer
// expect: 12
mod geo {
    pub fn area(w: int, h: int) -> int { w * h }
}

use geo::area

fn main() {
    println("${area(3, 4)}")
}
```

```windjammer,test
fn square(x: int) -> int { x * x }

@test
fn squares() {
    assert_eq(square(4), 16)
}

@test_cases([(2, 4), (3, 9)])
fn table(x: int, expected: int) {
    assert_eq(square(x), expected)
}
```

### Reading input and arguments

Programs that read standard input should use one spelling that behaves the same under `wj run --interpret` and `wj build`:

```windjammer,parse
use std::fs
use std::env

let text = fs::read_to_string("/dev/stdin").unwrap_or("")
for line in text.lines() {
    println(line)
}
for a in env::args() {
    println(a)
}
```

`io::stdin().read_line(..)` loops forever in compiled programs and `io::read_line()` is not implemented by the interpreter, so
prefer the `/dev/stdin` form. `env::args()` is an iterator: loop over it instead of slicing it.

### The 25 things agents get wrong first

1. `println!("{}", x)`: macros do not exist. Write `println("${x}")` (W0007/W0008, ADR-0014).
2. `vec![1, 2]`: write `[1, 2]`; `vec![0; n]` is `[0; n]`.
3. `#[derive(Debug, Clone)]`: the lexer rejects `#`. Derives are inferred; no attribute needed.
4. `&self`, `&mut self`, `&x` arguments: write `self`; ownership and borrows are inferred (W0001, W0004).
5. `.iter()` / `.iter_mut()`: delete them (W0003, an error in `wj build`).
6. `.unwrap()` / `.expect("..")`: use `match`, `?`, `unwrap_or`, `unwrap_or_default` (W0002).
7. `"lit".to_string()`: a literal is already a `string` (W0006). `.clone()` is usually unnecessary (W0005).
8. `i32`/`u64`/`usize` everywhere: use `int` and `float`; widths only at FFI/binary boundaries (ADR-0015).
9. A trailing `return x`: the last expression is the value; `return` is for early exit.
10. Semicolons: not needed.
11. `x as usize` indexing: `v[i]` accepts `int`. `as` still exists for explicit numeric/char casts.
12. `let x = 5; x += 1`: needs `let mut x` (ADR-0002). Parameters and receivers need no `mut`.
13. `{}` placeholders: use `"${x}"`; for literal braces nothing is needed, for a literal dollar write `$$`.
14. A string literal at the start of an interpolation, `"${"abc".len()}"`, fails to parse (open finding): bind it first with `let s = "abc"`.
15. `3.0` prints as `3`, `0.1 + 0.2` as `0.30000000000000004` (Rust's Display): use `${x:.2}` for fixed output.
16. Printing a `Result`/`Option`/`Vec`/struct needs `:?`; there is no auto Display for user types: define `fn to_string(self) -> string` and call it.
17. Range patterns (`1..=9 =>`), labeled `break 'outer`, and `if x is Some(v)` are not parsed yet: use guards, helper functions with `return`, `if let`.
18. `*counter += 1` as the first statement after a line ending in `)` is parsed as multiplication (open finding): use `.entry(k).and_modify(|c| *c += 1).or_insert(1)`.
19. `char::to_uppercase()` returns an iterator: use `to_ascii_uppercase()` for a char.
20. `HashMap` iteration order is unspecified: sort the keys; use `BTreeMap` for ordered output.
21. `mem::swap(&mut a, &mut b)` fails the borrow lint: use `v.swap(i, j)` or a temp.
22. `string.len()` is bytes, `.chars().count()` is characters; slicing is by bytes: `s[1..4]` (no `&`).
23. `x / y` on `int` truncates toward zero and `%` keeps the sign of the dividend; overflow panics (exit 101).
24. No ternary, no `while let` on non-patterns, no `async`/threads/`Rc`/`RefCell`/`impl Drop` in the interpreter (exit 2): use `wj build` for those.
25. Declaring success from `wj check` alone: always `wj run --interpret` (or `wj test --interpret`) to see behaviour.

### What not to write

Each of these is flagged by `wj check` (the block must produce a diagnostic):

```windjammer,bad
fn main() {
    let v = vec![1, 2, 3]
    println!("sum = {}", v.iter().sum::<i32>())
}
```

```windjammer,bad
fn first(v: &Vec<int>) -> int {
    v.get(0).unwrap()
}

fn main() {
    println("${first(&[1])}")
}
```

<!-- should_fail: Rust attribute syntax `#[derive]` is rejected (use `@derive`) -->
```windjammer,should_fail,bad
##[derive(Debug, Clone)]
struct P { x: int }

fn main() {
    println("${P { x: 1 }:?}")
}
```

### Compiled path gaps (be honest with the user)

`wj run --interpret` is the reference for behaviour. `wj build` additionally runs rustc: today about half of
`examples/verified` compiles and matches (`// rust: ok`); the rest carry a recorded `// rust: gap` reason in the
header. Known classes: adapter chains on a collection without `.iter()` (emitted as `v.map(..)` on a `Vec`),
integer-width inference between `i32` and `i64` in mixed expressions, `HashMap` indexing with `&str` keys,
inline `mod` plus `use` duplicates. Annotate numeric accumulators that start as a bare literal and later mix with `int` values (`let mut v: int = 0`, `let mut n: int = 0`): an
unannotated `let mut v = 0` can be emitted as `i32` and fail `wj build` with `mismatched types ... expected i64, found i32` while the
interpreter runs it. If `wj build` fails on other code the interpreter runs, report it with the smallest repro; do not contort the source.

### Where to look next

`wj docs <terms>` searches this guide, the cheat sheets (`cheatsheet_from_rust.md`, `_python`, `_go`, `_typescript`),
built-in methods, stdlib signatures and the verified examples (`examples/verified/*.wj`, indexed by tag in
`manifest.json`). Design decisions: `docs/adr/0014`, `0015`, `docs/design/pipe-operator.md`, `docs/INTERPRETER.md`.

# Source: docs/reference/cli.md

## `wj` command-line reference

Generated from the clap definitions in `src/bin/wj_cli_args.rs`.

### Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `wj new` | Create a new Windjammer project |
| `wj build` | Build a Windjammer project |
| `wj run` | Run a Windjammer program: interpreted by default (instant start), compiled when it needs to be |
| `wj repl` | Start the Windjammerscript REPL (interactive interpreter) |
| `wj test` | Run tests |
| `wj reduce` | Shrink a failing project to a minimal, anonymized reproduction (delta debugging) |
| `wj fmt` | Format Windjammer code |
| `wj fix` | Migrate deprecated surface syntax (`println!`, `vec![]`, `format!`, ...) to Windjammer forms |
| `wj lint` | Run Rust leakage linter on .wj files (W0001-W0004) |
| `wj check` | Type check without building |
| `wj add` | Add a dependency to wj.toml |
| `wj remove` | Remove a dependency from wj.toml |
| `wj update` | Update Windjammer to the latest version |
| `wj stats` | Show error statistics |
| `wj errors` | Browse the diagnostics of a file or project (summary by code, filterable) |
| `wj docs` | Search the offline docs index (stdlib signatures, built-in methods, idioms, verified examples, error codes); with no query, generate error documentation |
| `wj explain-ownership` | Explain inferred ownership, clones and numeric widths for a file (rule IDs and use sites) |
| `wj explain-effects` | Explain the effects (files, network, environment, processes, time, randomness, FFI) each function performs |
| `wj explain` | Explain an error code |
| `wj agent-index` | Generate agent index artifacts for MCP (errors, stdlib, spec JSON) |
| `wj shader-compile` | Compile .wjsl shader to WGSL (with type checking) |
| `wj validate-wjsl` | Validate WJSL shader files (transpile to WGSL and check for errors) |
| `wj clean` | Clean build artifacts and stale temp files |
| `wj cache` | Manage the shared Cargo target cache (outside application repos) |
| `wj cache path` | Print the shared (or --verify) Cargo target directory |
| `wj cache status` | Show cache sizes and free disk |
| `wj cache prune` | Reclaim space (old incremental; aggressive when disk is low) |
| `wj cache setup` | Write env.sh / env.ps1 for bare `cargo` invocations |
| `wj self-install` | Install wj and plugins to ~/.wj/bin/ and ensure PATH |

### `wj new`

Create a new Windjammer project

```text
Usage: wj new [OPTIONS] <NAME>
```

| Argument | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<NAME>` | NAME |  | Project name |
| `-t`, `--template` | TEMPLATE | cli | Project template (cli, web, lib, wasm) |

### `wj build`

Build a Windjammer project

```text
Usage: wj build [OPTIONS] <FILE>
```

| Argument | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<PATH>` | FILE |  | Path to .wj file or directory |
| `-o`, `--output` | DIR |  | Output directory (default: ./build) |
| `-r`, `--release` | RELEASE |  | Build in release mode |
| `-t`, `--target` | TARGET | rust | Target platform (rust, javascript, wasm) |
| `--defer-drop` | MODE | auto | Defer drop optimization mode (auto, always, never) |
| `--defer-drop-threshold` | BYTES |  | Defer drop threshold in bytes (default: 102400 = 100KB) |
| `--tree-shake` | TREE_SHAKE |  | Enable tree shaking (dead code elimination) |
| `--source-maps` | SOURCE_MAPS |  | Generate source maps |
| `--check` | CHECK |  | Run cargo build after transpilation and show errors |
| `--raw-errors` | RAW_ERRORS |  | Show raw Rust errors instead of translated Windjammer errors |
| `--fix` | FIX |  | Automatically apply fixes for fixable errors |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | VERBOSE |  | Show verbose error output (includes all notes and suggestions) |
| `-q`, `--quiet` | QUIET |  | Show only error count (suppress detailed output) |
| `--filter-file` | PATH |  | Filter errors by file path |
| `--filter-type` | TYPE |  | Filter errors by type (error, warning) |
| `--library` | LIBRARY |  | Library mode: exclude test main() functions from output |
| `--module-file` | MODULE_FILE |  | Auto-generate mod.rs with pub mod declarations and re-exports |
| `--no-cargo` | NO_CARGO |  | Skip cargo build after transpilation (transpile only) |
| `--no-lint` | NO_LINT |  | Disable Rust leakage linter warnings (style, .unwrap(), .iter(), etc.) |
| `--no-generate-cargo-toml` | NO_GENERATE_CARGO_TOML |  | Skip Cargo.toml generation (use project-maintained manifest) |
| `--metadata` | NAME=PATH |  | External crate metadata for cross-crate type inference (NAME=PATH, repeatable) |
| `--json` | JSON |  | Output diagnostics as machine-readable JSON (for agent/IDE consumption) |
| `--ir-shadow-validate` | IR_SHADOW_VALIDATE |  | Run IR shadow validation (compare solver results against legacy analyzer). Discrepancies are reported as errors instead of warnings (CI gate) |

### `wj run`

Run a Windjammer program: interpreted by default (instant start), compiled when it needs to be

```text
Usage: wj run [OPTIONS] [PATH] [ARGS]...
```

| Argument | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<PATH>` | PATH |  | A .wj file or a directory; omitted: the project containing the current directory (wj.toml) |
| `<ARGS>` | ARGS |  | Arguments to pass to the program |
| `--bin` | NAME |  | Binary to run (`[[bin]]` in wj.toml, cmd/<NAME>/main.wj or src/bin/<NAME>.wj) |
| `-t`, `--target` | TARGET | rust | Target platform (rust, javascript, wasm); non-rust targets always compile |
| `--interpret` | INTERPRET |  | Interpreter only: never fall back to the compiled path (exit 2 on an unsupported feature) |
| `--compiled` | COMPILED |  | Transpile to Rust and run with cargo (the release path), skipping the interpreter |
| `--release` | RELEASE |  | Like --compiled, with optimizations |
| `--watch` | WATCH |  | Re-run on every source change (restarts long-running programs) |
| `--hot` | HOT |  | Interpret and apply edits to function bodies while the program runs, keeping its state (preview, ADR-0021) |
| `--sched-seed` | N | 0 | Interpreted runs: thread schedule seed (0 = FIFO run-to-block; N explores another reproducible interleaving at every synchronisation point) |
| `--hash-seed` | N | 0 | Interpreted runs: perturb HashMap/HashSet iteration order (0 = key order; N = a reproducible shuffle) to expose programs that depend on Rust's unspecified hash order (ADR-0021 D6) |
| `--engine` | ENGINE | resolved | Interpreted runs: `resolved` (default: compiled closures, ADR-0020; functions outside its subset run in the tree walker) or `walker` (the tree walker only, the reference semantics) |
| `--no-lint` | NO_LINT |  | Interpreted runs: do not refuse the program for Rust-leakage lints (W####, such as `.unwrap()`); real compile errors still refuse it |
| `--deterministic-time` | DETERMINISTIC_TIME |  | Interpreted runs: no real clock; time starts at a fixed instant and only `sleep` moves it |
| `--allow-network` | ALLOW_NETWORK |  | Interpreted runs: allow plain http:// client requests (default: the http client refuses) |
| `--mock-http` | FILE |  | Interpreted runs: answer http client calls from a JSON file of canned responses |
| `--sandbox` | SANDBOX |  | Interpreted runs: ignore the project's grants and start from an empty one (only time, random and console); add authority with --allow (ADR-0021) |
| `--allow` | EFFECT[=RESOURCE] |  | Interpreted runs: grant an effect, e.g. `--allow net.connect=api.example.com`, `--allow fs.read=./data/**`, `--allow env.read=HOME`, `--allow process=git` (repeatable) |
| `--caps` | MODE | warn | Interpreted runs without a [capabilities] table: `warn` (default) runs outside-the-profile calls with a warning, `enforce` stops them (exit 126), `off` disables the gate |
| `--defer-drop` | MODE | auto | Defer drop optimization mode (auto, always, never) |
| `--defer-drop-threshold` | BYTES |  | Defer drop threshold in bytes (default: 102400 = 100KB) |

### `wj repl`

Start the Windjammerscript REPL (interactive interpreter)

```text
Usage: wj repl
```

### `wj test`

Run tests

```text
Usage: wj test [OPTIONS] [PATH]
```

| Argument | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<PATH>` | PATH |  | Directory or file containing tests (defaults to current directory) |
| `-f`, `--filter` | FILTER |  | Run only tests matching this pattern |
| `--nocapture` | NOCAPTURE |  | Show output from passing tests |
| `--parallel` | PARALLEL | true | Run tests in parallel (default: true) |
| `--json` | JSON |  | Output results as JSON for tooling |
| `--library` | LIBRARY | true | Compile the library under test (default when `src/` has `.wj` files) |
| `--module-file` | MODULE_FILE |  | Generate scoped `mod.rs` layout after transpile (same as `wj build --module-file`) |
| `-o`, `--output` | DIR |  | Output directory for library compile (default: temp `{lib}/`) |
| `--use-build-dir` | DIR |  | Use a pre-built outbound tree instead of recompiling the library |
| `--use-project-cargo` | USE_PROJECT_CARGO |  | Merge `[dependencies]` from project root `Cargo.toml` into the test library crate |
| `--no-runtime-copy` | NO_RUNTIME_COPY |  | Use a Cargo path dependency for windjammer-runtime (no recursive copy into temp). Also the default when `wj.toml` declares a path dep on `windjammer-runtime` |
| `--copy-runtime` | COPY_RUNTIME |  | Force copying windjammer-runtime into the temp tree (overrides path-dep inference) |
| `--runtime-path` | PATH |  | Explicit path to windjammer-runtime (with `--no-runtime-copy`) |
| `--no-generate-cargo-toml` | NO_GENERATE_CARGO_TOML |  | Skip auto-generated Cargo.toml for library compile |
| `--list` | LIST |  | List discovered test files and functions, then exit without compiling |
| `--allow-empty` | ALLOW_EMPTY |  | Exit 0 when no tests are found (default: finding none is an error) |
| `--interpret` | INTERPRET |  | Run tests (`@test` / `test_*` in `*_test.wj`) in the interpreter: no cargo, no rustc |
| `--watch` | WATCH |  | Re-run the tests on every source change |
| `--doc` | DOC |  | Run only the doctests (```wj examples in `///` doc comments) |
| `--compiled` | COMPILED |  | Also build and run each doctest through the Rust backend (default: interpreter only) |

### `wj reduce`

Shrink a failing project to a minimal, anonymized reproduction (delta debugging)

```text
Usage: wj reduce [OPTIONS] --oracle <SPEC> --output <DIR> <PATH>
```

| Argument | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<PATH>` | PATH |  | Project directory or .wj file to reduce |
| `--oracle` | SPEC |  | Bug oracle: `rustc-error E0308[:regex]`, `panic` (alias `crash`), `miscompile`, or `cmd '<shell>'` (exit 0 = bug present) |
| `-o`, `--output` | DIR |  | Output directory for the minimal project and repro.md |
| `--jobs` | N | 2 | Candidates evaluated in parallel |
| `--seed` | N | 0 | Seed for the deterministic candidate order |
| `--max-steps` | N | 5000 | Maximum number of oracle runs |
| `--time-budget` | SECS | 3600 | Wall-clock budget for the reduction search, in seconds |
| `--candidate-timeout` | SECS | 300 | Timeout for a single oracle run, in seconds |
| `--keep-names` | KEEP_NAMES |  | Accept a partially anonymized result when some names cannot be renamed without losing the bug |
| `--wj-bin` | WJ |  | Compiler binary used by the oracles (default: this executable) |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | VERBOSE |  | Print progress counts to stderr (never source text) |

### `wj fmt`

Format Windjammer code

```text
Usage: wj fmt [OPTIONS] [PATH]...
```

| Argument | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--check` | CHECK |  | Check formatting without applying changes (non-zero exit if changes are needed) |
| `--rust` | RUST |  | Format generated Rust crates with `cargo fmt --all` instead of .wj files |
| `<PATHS>` | PATH |  | Files or directories to format (default: current directory); `-` reads stdin |

### `wj fix`

Migrate deprecated surface syntax (`println!`, `vec![]`, `format!`, ...) to Windjammer forms

```text
Usage: wj fix [OPTIONS] <PATH>
```

| Argument | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<PATH>` | PATH |  | File or directory to rewrite in place |
| `--check` | CHECK |  | Do not write; exit non-zero if any file would change |
| `--docs` | DOCS |  | Also migrate ```windjammer / ```wj code fences in .md files |

### `wj lint`

Run Rust leakage linter on .wj files (W0001-W0004)

```text
Usage: wj lint [OPTIONS] <PATH>
```

| Argument | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<PATH>` | PATH |  | File or directory to lint |
| `--strict` | STRICT |  | Fail on warnings (for CI) |

### `wj check`

Type check without building

```text
Usage: wj check [OPTIONS] [PATH]
```

| Argument | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<PATH>` | PATH |  | Path to .wj file or directory (default: current directory) |
| `--json` | JSON |  | Output diagnostics as machine-readable JSON (docs/diagnostics-schema.json) |
| `--watch` | WATCH |  | Re-check whenever a .wj file changes |
| `--fix` | FIX |  | Apply machine-applicable fixes (W0007/W0008 rewrites, `.as_str()` removal, ...) |

### `wj add`

| Argument | Value | Default | Description |

| `--json` | JSON |  | Print search results as JSON |
| `-o`, `--output` | OUTPUT | ./docs/errors | Output directory for generated docs |
| `-f`, `--format` | FORMAT | html | Format (html, markdown, json) |

# Source: docs/reference/targets.md

## Backend support matrix

Generated from `tests/conformance_programs/SUPPORT.toml` and the program corpus in `tests/conformance_programs/`. A listed pair must fail its oracle; the harness ratchets the list down.

| Backend | Corpus programs | Passing | Known unsupported |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rust` | 156 | 129 | 27 |
| `go` | 156 | 156 | 0 |
| `js` | 156 | 156 | 0 |

### Known-unsupported pairs by cause

| Backend | Cause | Programs |
|---|---|---|
| `rust` | mut-ref-to-int-parameters | 2 |
| `rust` | rust-closure-field-move | 1 |
| `rust` | rust-closure-if-tail | 1 |
| `rust` | rust-int-literal-width-inference | 11 |
| `rust` | rust-into-bound-param-borrowed | 1 |
| `rust` | rust-module-impl-self-type | 1 |
| `rust` | rust-optional-chain | 1 |
| `rust` | rust-std-runtime-crate-needed-by-rustc | 4 |
| `rust` | rust-str-vs-string-in-collect-and-concat | 2 |
| `rust` | rust-tail-none-cast | 2 |
| `rust` | rust-unsized-slice-binding | 1 |

# Source: docs/reference/keywords.md

## Keywords and operators

Generated from `src/lexer/keywords.rs` (pinned to the lexer by unit tests) and from the lexer itself.

### Reserved words

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `fn` | function item or function type |
| `let` | local binding |
| `mut` | mutable binding or mutable reference |
| `const` | compile-time constant |
| `static` | static item |
| `struct` | struct item |
| `enum` | enum item |
| `trait` | trait item |
| `impl` | implementation block |
| `match` | pattern match expression |
| `if` | conditional expression |
| `else` | alternative branch of `if` |
| `for` | loop over an iterator |
| `in` | separator in `for pat in expr` |
| `while` | conditional loop |
| `loop` | unconditional loop |
| `return` | return from a function |
| `break` | leave a loop |
| `continue` | next loop iteration |
| `use` | import |
| `mod` | module declaration |
| `extern` | foreign declaration |
| `thread` | `thread { }` block |
| `async` | async function or block |
| `await` | await a future |
| `defer` | run a statement at scope exit |
| `pub` | public visibility |
| `self` | the receiver value |
| `unsafe` | unsafe block or function |
| `as` | type cast |
| `where` | trait-bound clause |
| `type` | type alias or associated type |
| `dyn` | trait object |

### Built-in type names

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `int` | default signed integer type |
| `int32` | 32-bit signed integer |
| `uint` | default unsigned integer type |
| `float` | default floating-point type |
| `bool` | boolean type |
| `string` | owned string type |

### Literals and wildcard

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `true` | boolean literal |
| `false` | boolean literal |
| `_` | wildcard pattern |

### Soft keywords (identifiers outside their position)

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Self` | the implementing type (lexes as an identifier) |
| `bound` | `bound Alias = Trait + ...` item (identifier elsewhere) |

### Operators and punctuation

Every punctuation string of up to three characters that the lexer turns into exactly one token.

| Lexeme | Token |
|---|---|
| `!` | Bang |
| `%` | Percent |
| `&` | Ampersand |
| `(` | LParen |
| `)` | RParen |
| `*` | Star |
| `+` | Plus |
| `,` | Comma |
| `-` | Minus |
| `.` | Dot |
| `/` | Slash |
| `:` | Colon |
| `;` | Semicolon |
| `<` | Lt |
| `=` | Assign |
| `>` | Gt |
| `?` | Question |
| `@` | At |
| `[` | LBracket |
| `]` | RBracket |
| `^` | Caret |
| `{` | LBrace |
| `\|` | Pipe |
| `}` | RBrace |
| `!=` | Ne |
| `%=` | PercentAssign |
| `&&` | And |
| `&=` | AndAssign |
| `*=` | StarAssign |
| `+=` | PlusAssign |
| `-=` | MinusAssign |
| `->` | Arrow |
| `..` | DotDot |
| `/=` | SlashAssign |
| `::` | ColonColon |
| `<-` | LeftArrow |
| `<<` | Shl |
| `<=` | Le |
| `==` | Eq |
| `=>` | FatArrow |
| `>=` | Ge |
| `>>` | Shr |
| `??` | QuestionQuestion |
| `^=` | XorAssign |
| `\|=` | OrAssign |
| `\|>` | PipeOp |
| `\|\|` | Or |
| `..=` | DotDotEq |
| `<<=` | ShlAssign |
| `>>=` | ShrAssign |
| `\|>?` | PipeTry |

# Source: crates/windjammer-mcp/tools/manifest.json

The `windjammer-mcp` server (`cargo build --release -p windjammer-mcp`, stdio by default) exposes:

- `parse_code` (analyze, stable): Parse Windjammer code and return AST structure
- `analyze_types` (analyze, stable): Perform type inference and analysis on Windjammer code
- `get_definition` (analyze, beta): Find the definition of a symbol at a given position
- `generate_code` (generate, beta): Generate Windjammer code from natural language description
- `explain_error` (knowledge, stable): Explain a Windjammer compiler error in plain English
- `search_workspace` (analyze, beta): Search for code patterns across the workspace
- `extract_function` (refactor, stable): Extract selected code into a new function
- `inline_variable` (refactor, stable): Inline a variable by replacing all uses with its value
- `rename_symbol` (refactor, stable): Rename a symbol with workspace-wide updates
- `generate_component` (generate, beta): Generate a Windjammer UI component with @component decorator
- `generate_game_entity` (generate, beta): Generate a game entity with @game decorator and ECS components
- `analyze_ssr_routing` (analyze, beta): Analyze SSR and routing configurations
- `get_language_info` (knowledge, stable): Get Windjammer compiler version, MCP version, and agent index metadata
- `query_diagnostics` (analyze, beta): Query structured compiler diagnostics for a scope (file, function, workspace)
- `query_effects` (analyze, beta): Query the resolved effect set and propagation chain for a function
- `check_code` (agent-loop, stable): Check Windjammer source (parse, lint, transpile) and return JSON diagnostics with spans and repair hints
- `run_code` (agent-loop, stable): Run Windjammer source in the interpreter (wj run --interpret); returns exit code, stdout, stderr
- `test_code` (agent-loop, stable): Run @test / test_* functions in the interpreter (wj test --interpret)
- `format_code` (agent-loop, stable): Format Windjammer source with the canonical formatter
- `docs_search` (knowledge, stable): Search offline docs: stdlib signatures, built-in methods, idioms, verified examples, error codes
- `insert_statement` (patch, beta): Insert a Windjammer statement at a given location with optional validation
- `change_type` (patch, beta): Change a type annotation at a given location in a source file


---

# Source: docs/known-gaps.md

## Known gaps

Ranked list of what is missing or wrong relative to what the documentation, RFCs and README promise. Source: the architecture
audit in [ARCHITECTURE_IMPROVEMENT_PLAN.md](ARCHITECTURE_IMPROVEMENT_PLAN.md) section 6, re-verified against the code on 2026-10-10.
Individual compiler bugs are not listed here ([ADR-0013](adr/0013-bug-triage-tracker.md)).

Status values: **Open** (nothing wired), **Partial** (some of it works), **Decision needed** (blocked on an ADR).

| Rank | Gap | Status | Evidence (today) | Work / decision |
|------|-----|--------|------------------|-----------------|
| 1 | Ownership, clone and numeric-width correctness is not owned by one component; blocks every dogfood project | Partial | Analyzer, IR solver and post-IR patches all decide ownership; width decided in 11 places; Rust-only solver consumption | Plan WP 6-9; [ADR-0001](adr/0001-ownership-truth.md) |
| 2 | No native diagnostics: type/borrow errors come from rustc and are translated; `compile_error!` emitted for unresolved boundary signatures | Partial | `src/error_mapper.rs`; IR doc "missing boundary signature" | [ADR-0005](adr/0005-error-strategy.md); needs name resolution (WP 6-7) |
| 3a | `.wj` formatter | Open | `wj fmt` runs `cargo fmt --all` (`src/cli/fmt.rs`) | Formatter work package (in progress elsewhere) |
| 3b | Real `wj check` | Partial | `wj check [--json] [--watch] [--fix]` runs the front end only (`src/check/`); catches names, arity, literal types, fields, mutability, lints; moves, borrows, traits, unknown methods, match exhaustiveness and operand types still need rustc and are translated (`src/diagnostics/rustc_text.rs`) | ADR-0005; [DIAGNOSTICS.md](DIAGNOSTICS.md) |
| 3c | `wj watch`, `wj doc`, `wj publish` | Open | No such subcommands in `src/bin/wj_cli_args.rs` (`wj docs` generates error docs only) | Roadmap "Then" list |
| 3d | `wj eject` on the main CLI | Partial | `eject` exists only on the older `windjammer` binary (`src/cli_args.rs`, `src/ejector.rs`) | ADR-0012 (move into `wj` or drop the promise) |
| 4 | Dependencies: path/git build in dependency order, lock file; registry deferred | Partial | `DependencySpec` has path/git; `src/package/` has manifest parsing only; no `wj.lock` | [ADR-0010](adr/0010-package-source-of-truth.md), [WJ-PKG-01](proposals/rfcs/WJ-PKG-01-package-management.md) |
| 5 | Concurrency: one coherent surface across backends; `async expr`/`spawn expr` do not parse; `go`/`chan::new()` were advertised but never existed | Decision needed | `AsyncCall`/`SpawnCall` never constructed; `thread {}`, `async fn`, `<-` do parse | [ADR-0004](adr/0004-concurrency-surface.md), [WJ-CONC-01](proposals/rfcs/WJ-CONC-01-async-concurrency.md) |
| 6a | Taint errors do not fail the build | Partial | Only `src/diagnostics/` consumes `taint_errors` | [ADR-0009](adr/0009-security-enforcement.md) |
| 6b | `.wj-capabilities.lock` not wired | Open | `src/ir/capability_lock.rs` unused by the CLI | ADR-0009, ADR-0010 |
| 6c | Unknown external calls have no effect classification; effects checked only with `[app_capabilities]` | Partial | `src/output_generation.rs` | ADR-0009, ADR-0012 |
| 7a | Go and JavaScript backends do not consume the IR | Open | `let _ir = ...prepare_ir_context(...)` in both generators | Plan WP 11; [ADR-0007](adr/0007-target-tiers-conformance.md) |
| 7b | Conformance suite runs only the Rust path | Partial | `tests/conformance/run_conformance_tests.sh` | ADR-0007 |
| 7c | Stdlib is Rust-host-only; no portability tags | Open | `std/*.wj` over `windjammer-runtime` | [ADR-0008](adr/0008-stdlib-portability.md) |
| 8 | Optimizer disabled; performance and economics claims unmeasured | Decision needed | `src/compiler_database.rs` `optimize_program`; no `wj optimize`/`wj economics` | [ADR-0006](adr/0006-optimizer-fate.md), [WJ-PERF-01](proposals/rfcs/WJ-PERF-01-economic-efficiency.md) |
| 9 | RFC features (comptime, const generics, `owned`) | Not started | No tokens/syntax; only `ConstEval::Comptime` IR scaffolding | [ADR-0003](adr/0003-owned-keyword.md), [WJ-LANG-02](proposals/rfcs/WJ-LANG-02-mojo-feature-analysis.md) |

### Language-surface questions the code and docs disagree on
| Question | State | ADR |
|----------|-------|-----|
| Is `let mut` required? | Docs say yes; codegen infers `mut` for mutated locals and parameters | [ADR-0002](adr/0002-local-mutability.md) |
| Does ternary `c ? a : b` exist? | RFC says implemented; parser removed it | WJ-SYN-02 row in the [RFC table](proposals/rfcs/README.md) |
| Are `use ... as` aliases and `std::http.client` submodule syntax supported? | Old docs said "future"; not verified in tests | [MODULE_SYSTEM.md](MODULE_SYSTEM.md) |
